question: Lorry drivers were filmed texting at the wheel. Each time they texted, how long did their eyes stay off the road?
answer: About 4.6 seconds in every 6, in a Virginia Tech study for US regulators. At 90 km/h that is 115 metres driven blind, longer than a football pitch. Car makers are asked to design screens so no glance needs more than 2 seconds: glances longer than that roughly doubled crash risk.
move: Count a glance in metres travelled, not in seconds lost.
ask: How far did I travel the last time I looked at my phone while driving?
reference: Olson, Hanowski, Hickman & Bocanegra, Driver Distraction in Commercial Vehicle Operations, FMCSA-RRR-09-042, 2009; NHTSA, Visual-Manual Driver Distraction Guidelines for In-Vehicle Electronic Devices, 2013; Klauer et al., The Impact of Driver Inattention on Near-Crash/Crash Risk, DOT HS 810 594, 2006
